samples.summary: Enter at offset 0 of a bulleted heading strands the remembered level on the empty leading bullet; the heading's text loses it (asymmetric with a plain heading)
samples.evidence: In `Doc.splitBlock`, a `list-item` always yields `newType = 'list-item'` (line 330), and `applySplitBlock` deletes `after.headingLevel` whenever `newBlockType !== 'heading'` (block-helpers.ts:256). So splitting a bulleted heading at offset 0 gives: `before` = empty list-item that KEEPS `headingLevel`, `after` = list-item holding the entire original heading text with NO `headingLevel`. Un-bulleting the text then produces a plain paragraph — exactly the Heading-2-downgrade the change set out to fix. The plain-heading path is deliberately not asymmetric: for `type === 'heading'` with `offset < blockText.length` the new block is also a `heading` (lines 332-337), so real headings survive an Enter at offset 0. The Yorkie store has the same asymmetry (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2140 only copies the level when `newBlockType === 'heading'`). The new tests only cover splitting at the END of the text (list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts 'splitting a bulleted heading leaves the new bullet plain'), so offset 0 is unguarded.

samples.summary: Multi-block paste into an empty bulleted list item collapses head and tail into the same block, scrambling the pasted content
samples.evidence: `insertBlocks` multi-block branch does `const tailBlockId = this.docSplitBlock(pos.blockId, pos.offset)` (line 3596) and then treats `pos.blockId` as the head and `tailBlockId` as a distinct tail. But `Doc.splitBlock` short-circuits for an empty list item — `if (block.type === 'list-item' && blockText.length === 0) { setBlockType(...); return blockId; }` (document.ts:303-307, a branch this diff edits) — returning the SAME id, so `tailBlockId === pos.blockId`. The head write (lines 3603-3610) appends `firstPasted`'s inlines, middle blocks are inserted after it (3621-3625), and then lines 3628-3640 re-read that same block as `tailBlock` and splice `lastPasted` at offset 0, producing `lastPasted + firstPasted` in one block with the middle blocks after it, plus type/style/headingLevel taken from `lastPasted`. The new test only covers a SINGLE-block paste into an emptied bulleted heading, so this path is untested. (Pre-existing, but the empty-list-item exit branch is directly modified here and the new `headingLevel` bookkeeping runs through it.)

samples.summary: Multi-block paste inside a bulleted heading overwrites the destination's own remembered level with the pasted block's
samples.evidence: `headBlock.headingLevel = pastedHeadingLevel(firstPasted, headOwnTextLen)` unconditionally replaces the head block's attribute. When the caret sits inside a bulleted heading (list-item with `headingLevel: 2`) and the pasted first block is an ordinary paragraph/list-item, the head block keeps its own heading text but its `headingLevel` becomes `undefined`, so un-bulleting it later yields a paragraph — the same silent heading downgrade the change fixes elsewhere. The new `pastedHeadingLevel` helper only guards against IMPORTING a foreign memory; it never guards the destination's existing one. Same shape at line 3636 for the tail block.

samples.summary: DOCX export drops a bulleted heading's remembered level, so export→import silently flattens it
samples.evidence: `block.type === 'heading' ? block.headingLevel : undefined` means a `list-item` carrying a remembered level exports with no `w:pStyle w:val="HeadingN"`. Re-importing (docx-style-map.ts:137-146 sets both `blockType` and `headingLevel` from the pStyle) therefore yields a plain bullet, and un-bulleting it gives body text instead of the original heading. The new test asserts this omission as intended ('DOCX export emits no Heading paragraph style'), but Word itself supports a bulleted heading, so the round trip is lossy for a document property the model now claims to preserve.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repo: document.ts:330-331 unconditionally sets newType='list-item' for a list-item split regardless of offset, while block-helpers.ts:256-258 deletes after.headingLevel for any non-'heading' target. So Enter at offset 0 of a non-empty bulleted heading (the empty-list-item early return at document.ts:303-307 does not apply) leaves `before` as an empty list-item retaining headingLevel and `after` holding all the heading text with the level stripped; unlistedBlockType (types.ts:337-344) then downgrades that text to a plain paragraph. The plain-heading path is not asymmetric (document.ts:332-337 keeps 'heading' when offset < length), confirming the inconsistency. The path is reachable with the raw cursor offset via TextEditor.docSplitBlock (text-editor.ts:389-393); the only offset>0 guards are in the unrelated table-insert callers (editor.ts:3257, 3276). Worse, undoing the Enter with Backspace merges after into before, and mergeDropsHeadingMemory (block-helpers.ts:279-285, applied at 293) matches the empty before block, deleting the remembered level permanently — real data loss. The design doc (docs/design/docs/docs.md:172-177) documents the drop rule but its rationale only covers the trailing-empty-bullet case, so it is not a guard. New tests only cover splitting at end of text (list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts:212-227). No refutation ground applies.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repo. text-editor.ts:3596 calls docSplitBlock and then treats pos.blockId as head (3599-3610) and tailBlockId as a distinct tail (3628-3640). docSplitBlock (text-editor.ts:389-393) merely forwards to Doc.splitBlock without normalizing the return. Doc.splitBlock (document.ts:297-307) short-circuits for an empty list-item — setBlockType then `return blockId` — returning the SAME id, so tailBlockId === pos.blockId. The head splice appends firstPasted inlines at headOwnTextLen, middle blocks are inserted after that same block (3620-3625), and the tail step then re-reads the same block and splices lastPasted at offset 0, yielding `lastPasted + firstPasted` in one block with middle blocks ordered after it and head metadata (type/style/headingLevel/listKind/listLevel/marker) overwritten by lastPasted. No guard blocks this: ensureEditableBlock (3502-3509) only handles horizontal-rule/page-break, and the callers at 1140, 1169, 1240 do not normalize an empty list-item caret. Pasting multi-block content into an empty bullet is an ordinary user action, so the corruption path is reachable — a real correctness/data-scrambling defect.
